..
Issued at 256 PM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Well-defined split flow pattern across 
western Canada is leaving the CONUS under the influence of the quasi-
zonal southern branch of that split.  Persistent upper low along the 
Pacific Northwest coast south of a strong short wave ridge (nearly 
+3 sigma 500mb height anomaly) across Alaska/Yukon Territory (a 
combined strongly negative PNA/EPO teleconnection).  Remnants of an 
old upper low northeast of Hawaii are approaching southern 
California and the Baja Peninsula.  Closer to home a pair of short 
wave troughs are tracking across northern Ontario/northwest 
Quebec...and a pair of weak PV anomalies over the Dakotas.  Drier 
air is advecting into the upper Lakes from the Midwest..displacing a 
narrow axis of around an inch and a quarter of precipitable water. 
This is accompanied by low/mid level cold air advection...with sub-
zero 850mb temperatures spreading into western Lake Superior. 
Surface cold front crossing the Great Lakes today...secondary cold 
front much farther north across northern Ontario and extending west 
into the Prairie Provinces.  

Split flow will consolidated right across the upper Lakes to end 
the week; northern branch short wave trough will cross the Lake 
Superior basin Friday while southern branch flow remains dominant. 
More amplified troughing along the west coast will try and push 
heights up across the region for the weekend.  Remnant short wave 
trough heading into Mexico today will eventually drift across the 
central/southern Plains Saturday and into the southeastern U.S. 
Sunday.  West coast troughing will eventually make its way into the 
nation's midsection for the first part of next week...but that means 
short wave ridging/higher heights across the Great Lakes.  Short 
wave trough may eventually try and make a run toward the region for 
mid to late week.  

High pressure over the northern Plains builds into Michigan/ 
Wisconsin by Friday morning.  Secondary cold front over northern 
Ontario will slip south tonight...pushed along by above mentioned 
northern branch short wave trough.  Looks like it will push through 
Upper Michigan overnight before dissipating Friday.  Surface high 
will propagate through the Great Lakes Saturday and into New England 
and the mid Atlantic Sunday.  This sets up southerly return flow 
into the Midwest and Great Lakes to start next week.  Inland 
propagating western trough looks to eventually spin up a lee cyclone 
over the central High Plains Monday...and because of the slow 
movement of the trough there may be several iterations of 
cyclogenesis/frontal waves through midweek along the north-south 
oriented baroclinic zone. 

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Some lake induced clouds/showers tonight/Friday: Thick Sc deck lies 
across Lake Superior and much of Upper Michigan at mid afternoon... 
replete with gravity wave ripples.  Persistent west-northwest fetch 
tonight will be longest into eastern Upper and extending into 
northern Lake Huron...longer fetch leading to a deeper CBL 
(inversion height around 800mb off Lake Superior).  Much shallower 
CBL the farther south you go down Lake Michigan with a much shorter 
fetch/loss of effective fetch.  Most showers should be confined to 
eastern Upper. 

Sunday rain chances?  Small but not zero...: For the weekend will 
need to watch short wave remnants moving into the Plains.  Deep 
moisture getting pulled north ahead of this "system"...some of this 
looks to get into Michigan Saturday night/Sunday though consensus 
PoPs are minimal through Sunday.  Saturday at least looks dry... 
we'll see how things trend for Sunday.   

Better rain threat beyond Monday: Rain chances should increase 
heading into Tuesday as more substantial system associated with slow 
moving western trough expected to bring stronger thermal/moisture 
advection into the Great Lakes.  Rain chances will continue through 
the midweek period.
